```{r setup}
source("../../R/fred.R")
source("../../R/generosity_data.R")
library(knitr)
```

We spend a lot of time on this site digging into what life costs. This week, for Thanksgiving, we wanted to look at
the other side of the ledger: what Americans **give**. The numbers are a nice reminder that, whatever the headlines say,
an awful lot of people are quietly showing up for each other.

## The short answer

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Americans gave a record **$`r giving_total_2025_b` billion** to charity in 2025, about **$`r formatC(giving_per_day_b, format = "f", digits = 1)` billion every day**.
**`r volunteers_m` million** people volunteered through an organization, giving **`r volunteer_hours_b` billion hours** of their time.
And **`r neighbors_helped_m` million**, more than half of us, helped a neighbor.
:::

## We give a lot of money

In 2025, total U.S. charitable giving crossed **$600 billion for the first time**, reaching **$`r giving_total_2025_b` billion**,
according to *Giving USA 2026*. That was up `r giving_growth_2025`% from the year before.

The biggest share didn't come from foundations or corporations. It came from **regular individuals: about
$`r giving_individuals_2025_b` billion**, roughly two-thirds of the total. That's checks to churches, donations to food banks,
gifts to schools and charities, and countless $20 contributions that add up.

## We give a lot of time

Money is only part of it. In the latest national survey by the Census Bureau and AmeriCorps:

```{r time table}
tribble(
  ~`What Americans did (Sept 2022 – Sept 2023)`, ~Number,
  "Formally volunteered through an organization", paste0(volunteers_m, " million people (", volunteer_rate, "% of those 16+)"),
  "Hours volunteered", paste(volunteer_hours_b, "billion"),
  "Economic value of that time", paste0("about $", volunteer_value_b, " billion"),
  "Informally helped a neighbor (errands, house-sitting, lending tools)", paste0(neighbors_helped_m, " million people (", neighbors_rate, "%)")
) %>% kable(align = "lr", caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau and AmeriCorps, Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement.")
```

To put **`r volunteer_hours_b` billion hours** in perspective: that's the same as about **`r formatC(fulltime_jobs_equiv_m, format = "f", digits = 1)` million people** working full time
for an entire year, for free.

## And volunteering is bouncing back

```{r trend chart}
#| fig-height: 3.5
ggplot(volunteer_trend, aes(factor(year), rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = c("#9AB0C4", "#9AB0C4", "#2A9D8F"), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(rate, "%")), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 35), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Share who volunteered")
```

The pandemic knocked volunteering down hard. Between 2021 and 2023, it jumped from **23.2%** to **28.3%**, the biggest
increase since the government started tracking it in 2002. It's still a little below where it was before COVID, but it's
heading the right way. Some of the biggest gains came from Millennials and from people with lower incomes.

## The biggest giving day of the year is coming

**Giving Tuesday**, the Tuesday after Thanksgiving, has become a giving holiday of its own. In 2025, about
**`r giving_tuesday_2025_m` million Americans** gave a total of **$`r giving_tuesday_2025_b` billion in a single day**, a record.

This year it's **`r giving_tuesday_2026`**. If you want to join in, it doesn't have to be money: a few hours at a local food bank,
shelter, or school counts too. So does checking on a neighbor.

## The fine print

- **Giving totals** are estimates from *Giving USA*, published by the Giving USA Foundation with Indiana University's
  Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. They include giving by individuals, foundations, bequests, and corporations.
- **Volunteering figures** are from 2023, the latest national survey; new data is expected in 2026.
- **The "2019" volunteering rate** is calculated from the Census Bureau's statement that the 2023 rate was 1.7 points below
  pre-pandemic levels.
- One honest note: the *number* of people who give to charity has been slipping for several years, even as total dollars
  rise. More money is coming from fewer, larger donors.

## The bottom line

It's easy to feel like everyone is only looking out for themselves. The data says otherwise: hundreds of billions of
dollars, billions of hours, and tens of millions of small kindnesses between neighbors, every single year. That seems
like something worth being thankful for.

Happy Thanksgiving from SixtyEight95.

**How we did this.** Giving totals are from *Giving USA 2026: The Annual Report on Philanthropy for the Year 2025*.
Volunteering and neighbor-helping figures are from the U.S. Census Bureau and AmeriCorps Current Population Survey Civic
Engagement and Volunteering Supplement (September 2023). Giving Tuesday figures are from the GivingTuesday Data Commons.
